Spain as a single monarchy began with the union of the crowns of Castile and Aragon in 1479, under Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon, who had married ten years before. Within a century it ruled the first empire on which the sun never set.

The two crowns kept their own laws and parliaments; what joined them was the royal couple. 1492 was their great year. They took Granada, the last Muslim state of al-Andalus, ordered the expulsion of the Jews, and paid for Columbus's voyage to the Caribbean. The Spanish Inquisition, set up in 1478, policed the faith of converts.

The empire:

  • Conquest of the Aztecs by Cortés and of the Inca by Pizarro in the 1520s and 1530s.
  • Their grandson Charles V also inherited the Habsburg lands and the Low Countries.
  • Silver from Potosí and Mexico paid for wars across Europe and flowed on to China, partly via the Manila galleons.
  • Under Philip II Spain also ruled Portugal (1580 to 1640), but lost the Armada against England in 1588 and faced a long Dutch revolt.

The silver was spent faster than it came, and the crown went bankrupt several times; Genoese bankers lent against it. Decline set in during the 1600s. A Bourbon king took the throne in 1700, and the Spanish American colonies broke away in the 1810s and 1820s.

The 1900s brought the Spanish Civil War (1936 to 1939) and Franco's dictatorship until his death in 1975. A peaceful return to democracy followed under a restored king, and Spain joined the European Community in 1986.
